mem.t: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

lessons.title: Continuing Steadfastly in Prayer with One Accord
lessons.theme: The church was born out of a prayer meeting

v: All these with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer and supplication, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.

lessons.still: Imagine yourself in that upper room in Jerusalem, waiting with the hundred and twenty. No one is rushing to get things done; everyone is simply praying together. Quietly join them and say to the Lord, “Lord, I am willing to wait for you together with my brothers and sisters.”
teach: Before an orchestra begins, all the musicians tune together; if they are out of tune, no amount of skill produces anything but noise. Before Pentecost the early church “tuned up” in prayer — they “with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer,” waiting for the Holy Spirit the Father had promised.

The group in Acts 1:14 was diverse: the apostles, several women, Jesus' mother, and his brothers who had once not believed in him. What they shared was being “of one accord” and “steadfast.” After Pentecost the newborn church still “continued steadfastly in the apostles' teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer” — prayer was not an occasional activity but the rhythm of the church's life.

We often think of prayer as a private matter, but in Scripture prayer is also the breathing of the community. Here is the mindset change: praying in one accord is not adding up individual prayers; it is a group of people tuning together to the heart of God. Private prayer builds intimacy with God; united prayer builds a community that belongs to God.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Our one purpose — building God's kingdom system — was born in prayer. Being of one accord requires each person to live the self-emptied life: laying down our own agendas and tuning together to God's will. Pride makes everyone talk past each other; humility brings people into one accord, and the Holy Spirit works among them.
q: Who is God? — Why did God choose to pour out his Spirit on a group of people praying with one accord?
Who am I? — Is your prayer life more like a solo or an ensemble?
How shall I respond? — Which time of united prayer can you join or start this week?
lessons.jesus: Before his ascension Jesus told his disciples not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for what the Father had promised (Acts 1:4). He did not tell them each to go home and wait, but to wait together. The prayer the Lord taught also begins with “our”: “Our Father in heaven” — from the very start, prayer is a family matter.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often pray only for myself and seldom pray in one accord with my brothers and sisters. Make me willing to lay down my own agenda and pray steadfastly with your people, of one heart and mind. May your church be filled with you as we pray. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Check this week's prayer meetings at your church or small group and plan to attend
Send a message to a brother or sister: “Shall we pray together for five minutes?”
When you pray today, change “I” to “we”
lessons.noon: “They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.” — Lord, right now make prayer the rhythm of my life.

lessons.title: Two or Three in Agreement
lessons.theme: The Lord promises to be among two or three gathered in his name

v: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

lessons.still: Think of one or two people you could pray with, and in your heart bring them to your side. Quietly receive the Lord's promise: “There I am in the middle of them.” The Lord is standing among you — not far away in heaven.
teach: The light of one match is faint, but put two or three together and the flame grows strong enough to light a pile of wood. The Lord did not say we must wait for hundreds of people before we pray; he said “two,” “two or three” — the smallest unit of united prayer, so small that everyone can take part.

“Agreeing” is like several instruments sounding the same chord: not just agreeing on the same thing, but hearts tuned together toward God. “In my name” means gathering according to the Lord's heart and under his authority. These words come in the context of dealing with a brother who sins, which shows that united prayer is also closely tied to restoring relationships and keeping order in the community.

This promise is not a wishing well, as if God must comply once two people have agreed. The key is “in my name” — when two or three agree under the Lord's name, what they ask becomes more and more like the Lord's heart, and the Lord himself is among them. Here is the mindset change: the greatest reward of united prayer is not just answered prayer but the Lord's presence.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The best way for “2” spiritual companions in 235 to spend time together is to pray in agreement. If one of the two is self-ruled and insists on his own way, they cannot agree; if both are self-emptied and let Jesus reign, they can be of one heart and mind. Answered prayer is for Jesus to receive the glory, not for us to feel pleased with ourselves.
q: Who is God? — The Lord promises to be among two or three. How near is this Lord to you?
Who am I? — Have you and your spiritual companion ever prayed together?
How shall I respond? — With whom will you arrange a “two or three” time of united prayer this week?
lessons.jesus: Jesus took Peter, James and John up the mountain to pray (Luke 9:28), and “as he was praying,” the appearance of his face changed. He often prayed together with a few disciples, letting them see with their own eyes the glory of his fellowship with the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for promising to be among two or three. Give me companions to pray with in agreement, and help us lay down our own ideas and be of one accord in your name. What we long for most is not only answered prayer but your presence. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Arrange with your spiritual companion to pray together for fifteen minutes this week
Each share one prayer request, and pray for one another
lessons.noon: “For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.” — Lord, right now you are here among us.

lessons.title: The Power of the Prayer Meeting
lessons.theme: When the church prays earnestly, prison doors open and believers are filled with the Spirit

v: Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.
When they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were gathered together. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.

lessons.still: Think of people around you who are “locked in prison” — trapped by illness, hardship or bondage. Quietly bring their names before the Lord. Then ask the Lord to help you see that the praying community you belong to is a channel through which God works.
teach: When a dam is full and the sluice gates open, the water drives the turbines and lights up a whole city. The prayer meeting is often seen as the least popular gathering: few people, long hours, not much buzz. In fact it is the church's “power station” — God's power is displayed through united prayer.

In Acts 12 James had been killed and Peter imprisoned; the situation was hopeless. “But constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him” — that one word “but” turned everything around. The angel of the Lord led Peter out of prison, while the people praying were gathered in Mary's house. In Acts 4, after the disciples were threatened, they prayed together, “the place was shaken,” and they were filled with the Holy Spirit and “spoke the word of God with boldness.” They did not ask for the danger to disappear; they asked for boldness.

Interestingly, when Peter knocked at the door, those praying at first did not believe it was him (12:15)! God's answer was bigger than their faith. Here is the mindset change: the power of prayer does not lie in how perfect our faith is, but in the God who hears prayer. What God values is a group of people willing to gather and come before him earnestly together.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The prayer meeting is a community act of “letting Jesus reign” — admitting we are powerless and handing the situation over to God. The focus is not how frightening the circumstances are but that Jesus is in control. In a crisis, the church does not first rely on its own solutions but prays first; this is living from the heart by the Spirit.
q: Who is God? — In the darkness of James's death and Peter's imprisonment, how did God answer the church's prayer?
Who am I? — Do you see the prayer meeting as optional, or as the church's power station?
How shall I respond? — For which person “in prison” could you invite others to pray together this week?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus cleansed the temple he quoted Scripture: “My house shall be called a house of prayer” (Matthew 21:13). In his heart, God's house is first and foremost a place of prayer. He also promised that whatever his disciples ask in his name he will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son (John 14:13).
lessons.pray: Lord, revive our prayer meetings, and forgive us for so often treating prayer as optional. We pray earnestly for brothers and sisters caught in hardship; please act on their behalf. And fill us with the Holy Spirit, so that we speak your word with boldness. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Attend this week's prayer meeting at your church or small group
For a brother or sister in difficulty, invite two or three others to pray together
Write down one prayer request, then wait for and record God's answer
lessons.noon: “But constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.” — Lord, right now I cry out to you for those caught in hardship.

lessons.title: Praying for the Kingdom
lessons.theme: The scope of prayer widens from my needs to God's kingdom

v: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,
for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.

lessons.still: Slowly pray the first three lines of the Lord's Prayer, pausing after each line to take a deep breath. When you reach “Let your Kingdom come,” quietly imagine God's kingdom coming to your home, your city, your nation.
teach: Many people's prayers are like a shopping list: health, a job, the children… All of these are fine to ask for, but if that is all our prayer contains, it is like a window that only looks out on our own backyard. The Lord's Prayer opens a large window for us, so that we can see God's kingdom.

The Lord's Prayer puts God first and people second: first “may your name be kept holy,” then “let your Kingdom come” and “let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven,” and only then our daily bread. Paul likewise urged Timothy that “first of all, petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,” including “kings and all who are in high places.” Praying for the kingdom means asking that God's will be done in the church, in our cities and among the nations.

Praying for the kingdom can have specific scopes: for the church's pastors and workers, for the leaders and society of our city, for our nation's government, for unreached peoples, for the persecuted church. Here is the mindset change: prayer is not only God meeting my needs; it is me taking part in God's work. When we pray for the kingdom, our own needs actually find their proper place.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God's kingdom system means fulfilling the Lord's Prayer — hallowing his name, his kingdom coming, his will done on earth as in heaven; the kingdom, the power and the glory all belong to God. A change of perspective: from the earthly to the heavenly, from the temporary to the eternal. Praying for the kingdom is letting Jesus reign over all things.
q: Who is God? — God “desires all people to be saved.” How wide is the heart of his kingdom?
Who am I? — How much of your prayer list is for God's kingdom?
How shall I respond? — Which area of the kingdom (church, city, nation, the nations) will you pray for regularly this week?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus saw the crowds harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd, he said to his disciples, “Pray therefore that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:38). He did not only do the work himself; he taught his disciples to pray for the needs of God's kingdom.
lessons.pray: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy; may your kingdom come; may your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Widen the scope of my prayers, so that I intercede for the church, my city, my nation and all peoples. Yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make a kingdom prayer list covering the church, your city, your nation and the nations
Pray today for one of your nation's leaders
Pray for an unreached people group or a persecuted church
lessons.noon: “Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.” — Lord, right now reign in me.

lessons.title: Building Prayer Partnerships
lessons.theme: Holding up each other's hands, we overcome together

v: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.

lessons.still: Lift up both hands for a moment and feel your arms gradually grow heavy. As you lower them, ask the Lord to remind you of brothers and sisters whose “hands may be growing heavy,” and admit honestly, “Lord, I too need someone to hold up my hands.”
teach: Down in the valley Joshua was fighting; up on the hill Moses was lifting his hands. The outcome of the battle depended not on swords but on a pair of raised hands. But Moses was human, and his hands grew heavy. So Aaron and Hur brought a stone for him to sit on and held up his hands, one on each side — “His hands were steady until sunset.”

This is a picture of prayer partners: in spiritual warfare no one can keep their hands raised alone to the end. Aaron and Hur were not the main characters, yet they were key to the victory; they did not replace Moses, they held him up. Prayer partners are like that: when the other is weary, we hold them up in prayer until the victory is won.

This week we have walked through the early church's united prayer, the promise to two or three, the power of the prayer meeting, and praying for the kingdom. Today let us put it into practice by forming regular prayer partnerships — setting a time, sharing needs, praying for one another, and recording answers. Next week we will learn about the gifts of the Holy Spirit — how, like Aaron and Hur, each of us plays our part in the body of Christ and works together with others.
lessons.light: 321 Light: From the “2” spiritual companions to the “5” fellow soldiers of 235, everyone needs the support of prayer. Do not hurt people for the sake of tasks; hold people up for the sake of people. The humble admit they need support; the self-emptied are willing to be the unseen ones holding up the hands — the glory goes to God, not to ourselves.
q: Who is God? — God tied victory to a pair of hands held up by others. What does that show you about how he designed community?
Who am I? — Are you more like Moses, with heavy hands needing support, or like Aaron and Hur, able to hold others up?
How shall I respond? — With whom will you form a regular prayer partnership, supporting one another?
lessons.jesus: In the Garden of Gethsemane Jesus said to his disciples, “Stay here, and watch with me.” He longed for someone to pray with him, but the disciples fell asleep. Now “he always lives to make intercession for them” (Hebrews 7:25); he is the High Priest who forever holds up our hands.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you that you always live to intercede for me. I confess that I often try to hold on alone, and my hands have grown heavy. Give me prayer partners, and make me willing to be an Aaron or a Hur for others, holding up their hands in prayer until the victory is won. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Invite a companion to become your regular prayer partner
Agree on a weekly time to share prayer requests with each other
Start a prayer journal to record each other's needs and God's answers
lessons.noon: “Aaron and Hur held up his hands.” — Lord, right now I lift my hands in prayer for my companion.
